analysis.title: Intel Corp. (INTC): Servers very strong, but PC weakness likely to be a setback for the stock
key_insights: GS expects INTC to trade meaningfully lower after a solid 3Q26 print because 4Q guidance came in well below the Street, driven by a sharp PC market decline. GS says investor expectations were skewed positive going into the print.

3Q26 revenue was $16.5bn, below GS at $17.0bn and in line with the Street at $16.4bn. Gross margin was 44.1% (GS 42.7%, Street 41.9%), operating margin 19.6% (GS 17.9%) and non-GAAP EPS $0.52 (GS $0.47, Street $0.39).

By segment, CCG revenue of $8.1bn missed GS ($9.0bn) and the Street ($8.9bn). DCAI revenue of $7.3bn beat GS ($7.1bn) and the Street ($6.6bn). Intel Foundry revenue of $6.7bn beat GS ($6.1bn) and the Street ($6.0bn).

DCAI grew 17% QoQ and 78% YoY on general-purpose server demand and agentic AI. Intel expects server CPU units to grow over 30% in both 2026 and 2027 with higher ASPs, and a TAM of about $200bn by 2030. It expects mid-teens sequential DCAI growth in 4Q as more supply comes online, and it is still capacity constrained.

Management described a weaker PC environment extending into 2027, citing limited IT budgets, elevated inventories and memory constraints. Intel expects 2026 PC units down about 12% and another roughly 10% TAM decline in 2027, with weakness concentrated in 1H.
Client revenue is expected to fall about 20% QoQ in 4Q. The inventory correction extends through 1Q and possibly 2Q, on top of normal seasonality.

Foundry progress: Intel 3 costs improved 15% from 1Q and 18A costs are down about 40% since 1Q. 18A-P is on track with growing inbound external customer interest. The 14A 0.9 PDK is with select customers and the 1.0 PDK is expected in 1Q27. EMIB/EMIB-T packaging yields and capacity are improving.
4Q26 guidance midpoint: revenue $15.5bn (GS $18.0bn, Street $17.0bn), non-GAAP gross margin 38% (GS 43.6%, Street 42.5%), non-GAAP EPS $0.25 (GS $0.46, Street $0.43).
GS cut estimates by about 20% on average, mainly from lower CCG revenue and lower gross margins. 2027E revenue falls 9.0% to $73.2bn and 2027E EPS (excl. SBC) falls 21.9% to $2.15.

Rating stays Neutral. The 12-month price target drops to $100 from $150, using 25x P/E (down from 30x on lower peer multiples) on normalized EPS of $4.00 (down from $5.00). GS says AMD, NVDA and AVGO offer more favorable risk/reward than INTC.
GS sees upside optionality from Intel's role as a US champion in foundry, with near-term traction in advanced packaging and longer-term potential in wafer outsourcing.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $100 from $150 on a lower P/E multiple (25x from 30x) and lower normalized EPS ($4.00 from $5.00) after weak 4Q guidance and PC market weakness. GS expects the stock to trade meaningfully lower after the print.

sector_views.rationale: Intel expects 2026 PC units down about 12% and a further roughly 10% TAM decline in 2027, with inventory correction into 1H27 and memory constraints weighing on demand.
Agentic AI and general-purpose server demand are driving unit growth above 30% in 2026 and 2027 with higher ASPs. Intel is still supply constrained.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported revenue $16,513mn vs GS est $17,027mn and Street (Visible Alpha) $16,419mn. Revenue grew 2.4% QoQ and 20.9% YoY.

3Q26 non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) reported $0.52 vs GS est $0.47 and Street est $0.39. Gross margin (excl. SBC) reported 44.1% vs GS est 42.7% and Street est 41.9%. Operating margin reported 19.6% vs GS est 17.9% and Street est 16.1%. The text cites the Street operating margin as 16.5%, while Exhibit 1 shows 16.1%.

4Q26 guidance midpoint: revenue $15.5bn (range $15.0-16.0bn) vs GS est $18.0bn and Street est $17.0bn. Non-GAAP gross margin guided to 38% vs GS est 43.6% and Street est 42.5%. Non-GAAP EPS guided to $0.25 vs GS est $0.46 and Street est $0.43.

GS new estimates (excl. SBC): 2026E revenue $62.2bn (old $64.7bn), EPS $1.51 (old $1.65). 2027E revenue $73.2bn (old $80.4bn), EPS $2.15 (old $2.75). 2028E revenue $92.0bn (old $98.1bn), EPS $3.80 (old $4.70).
GS 2027E CCG revenue was cut 22.8% to $27.8bn. 2027E gross margin (excl. SBC) is 42.4%, down 302 bps from the prior 45.4%.
Intel expects client revenue to fall about 20% QoQ in 4Q26 and DCAI to grow mid-teens sequentially.
risk_factors: Downside risks to INTC: slower than expected ramp of advanced foundry nodes, and lower server CPU share.
Upside risks to INTC: increased traction for Intel Foundry services, better demand and share trends in server CPUs, and stronger margin improvement.
PC demand risk: limited IT budgets, elevated inventories and memory constraints, with the correction possibly lasting into 2Q27.
Intel's server CPU supply is constrained, which caps near-term DCAI growth.
vol_and_positioning: GS notes investor expectations going into the print were skewed positive on Server CPU strength, advanced packaging momentum and foundry node progress, which sets up a downside reset to Street estimates after the PC-driven guide.
